question: ISRO decided to open a Regional Academic Centre for Space at IIT ______ in December 2020.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Varanasi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• ISRO decided to open a Regional Academic Centre for Space at IIT Varanasi in December 2020.
 
• This initiative is aimed at creating an ecosystem to foster space technology research and innovation in collaboration with academic institutions.
 
• IIT Varanasi, also known as IIT BHU, has a rich history of academic excellence and research capabilities.
 
• The collaboration will focus on advanced research areas like satellite development, space exploration, and other cutting-edge space technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**

 
 
• ISRO is the space agency of the Government of India, headquartered in Bengaluru.
 
• It was founded on August 15, 1969, and is responsible for the planning and execution of space missions.
 
• ISRO has achieved significant milestones, including the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) and the Chandrayaan missions.
 
• It aims to harness space technology for national development while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration.
 
 
 
• **IIT (Indian Institutes of Technology)**
 
 
• IITs are autonomous public technical universities located across India.
 
• They are governed by the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961, which has declared them as institutions of national importance.
 
• IIT Varanasi, also known as IIT BHU, is one of the oldest engineering institutions in India, established in 1919 as Banaras Engineering College.
 
• IITs are renowned for their high academic standards, rigorous selection process, and contributions to research and development in various engineering and technology fields.
 
 
 
• **Regional Academic Centre for Space (RAC-S)**
 
 
• RAC-S is a collaborative initiative by ISRO to promote space technology research and innovation through academic institutions.
 
• These centers aim to strengthen the research capabilities of academic institutions by providing access to ISRO's resources and expertise.
 
• They focus on advanced research areas, including satellite development, space exploration, and space applications.
 
• The establishment of RAC-S at IIT Varanasi is part of ISRO's efforts to expand its collaboration with academic institutions across India.
